newsitem.title: GERMANY: Philippine Air plans more Europe flights.
newsitem.headline: Philippine Air plans more Europe flights.

text.p: Philippine Airlines (PAL) said it will expand flights to Europe substantially this autumn and next year.
Roberto Diaz de Rivera, the carrier's regional vice-president Europe, said loss-making PAL planned extra services to London, Frankfurt and possibly Paris in 1997.
Flights to Amsterdam and Rome could then be started in 1998, the Frankfurt-based manager told Reuters in an interview.

The PAL strategy was to build up frequent, direct services to European countries using new Airbus A340 aircraft in place of the previous, unviable Boeing 747-200 flights, which had to make several stops, he explained.
PAL launched separate three-times-a week flights to London and Paris last October with the six Frankfurt flights terminating in Germany.
De Rivera said: "There will be further expansion this year. We are targeting breakeven in 1998 and are optimistic we can make European operations profitable by 2000."
PAL will add a fourth weekly London-Manila flight from July 6 and a fifth service on October 5, and start a seventh Frankfurt flight on October 6, he added.
There was no decision yet on a fourth Paris flight, de Rivera said.
"Next year we plan to put on Amsterdam and Rome back on-line and we might combine them twice a week," he added.
De Rivera said the fortunes of the European flights could determine PAL's aim of returning to profit in 1998 since Europe currently contributed much of the carrier's losses.
The airline was seeing an upturn in passenger demand for tourist destinations such as Cebu and was also targeting the Philippine community in Europe, he added.
